name: Moses
epithet: The one who was sent back to the place he fled

stops.title: The Bush That Was Not Consumed

passage.a: Moses saw a bush burning without burning up. God called him to lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
passage.b: While tending a flock near Horeb, Moses saw a bush burning without being consumed. God called to him from the bush and sent him to Pharaoh to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
passage.c: Moses was tending his father-in-law Jethro’s flock near Horeb when he saw a bush burning without being consumed. God called to him from the bush and told him to remove his sandals because the ground was holy. God then sent Moses to Pharaoh to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.

learned.b: Moses was called from tending a flock to leading a people.
learned.c: At Horeb, an ordinary shepherd’s day became the beginning of a calling.

aliases: The bush that was not consumed
puzzles.textHint: It burns, but its branches are not consumed.
puzzles.moral: An ordinary place can become a place of calling.

passage.a: Moses and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh. They asked him to let the Israelites go. Pharaoh refused.
passage.b: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and asked him to let the Israelites hold a festival for God in the wilderness. Pharaoh said he did not know the Lord and refused to let Israel go.
passage.c: Moses and Aaron stood before Pharaoh and asked him to let the Israelites go into the wilderness to hold a festival for God. Pharaoh questioned why he should obey the Lord and refused their request. The encounter brought Moses’ calling into direct conflict with Egypt’s ruler.

learned.a: Moses and Aaron spoke, even when Pharaoh refused.
learned.b: Moses and Aaron brought their request to a ruler who refused.
learned.c: Moses and Aaron spoke before Pharaoh; his refusal set the struggle in motion.

puzzles.textHint: Egypt’s ruler refused Moses and Aaron’s request.
puzzles.moral: Power does not make a refusal wise.

stops.title: The Sea
stops.contentWarning: This story includes danger at sea. No violence is shown.

passage.a: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. God made a dry path. The Israelites walked through.
passage.b: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The Lord drove the sea back with a strong east wind through the night, and the Israelites crossed on dry ground, with water on both sides.
passage.c: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove it back with a strong east wind through the night. The waters divided, leaving dry ground. The Israelites went through the sea with a wall of water on their right and on their left.

learned.a: The Israelites crossed the sea on dry ground.
learned.b: A strong east wind opened a dry path through the sea.
learned.c: The people crossed on dry ground, with the waters standing on either side.

puzzles.textHint: The people crossed on dry ground between walls of water.
puzzles.moral: A way forward can appear where none seemed possible.
